text:
kamal: thinking about adding a header-based override for canary routing. idea: if X-Redwood-Route-Hint=canary we route 100% to canary for debugging sessions. want thoughts on telemetry, quotas, and safety.

sara: hmm that sounds useful for debugging. question: how does that interact with per-customer quotas? we don't want to bypass reserved capacity.

mike: +1 for debug use, but prefer a `session` param rather than header if it's user-facing. headers are great for infra tests tho.

andrew: telemetry concern: if we allow 100% header override we need to label those requests in metrics (route.override=header) so SLOs exclude them or we get skewed p95s.

linda: UX: in the console, can we show a small "forced traffic" badge and an audit log entry with the header value + who triggered it? :eyes:

kamal: good call. proposal update:

```json
{
  "match": {"path": "/v1/generate", "method": "POST"},
  "override": {"type": "header", "name": "X-Redwood-Route-Hint", "value": "canary"},
  "metadata": {"label": "header-forced-canary", "exclude_from_slo": true}
}
```

mike: API gateway note: we should require a token check for the header so only internal tooling can set it. otherwise customers or proxies could spoof.

sara: on quotas: keep accounting against the original tenant id, but flag billing metadata `forced_canary=true`. That way cost/usage doesn't get lost.

andrew: also add a sampling cap: only allow header-forced sessions up to N rps or M concurrent sessions per org to avoid accidental attack surface.

ops-bot: alert: adding header override without token check can bypass rate-limits (simulated test)

deploy-bot: staged rollout started for header-override feature on canary cluster (tag: header-override-2026-03)

linda: final UX ask: expose a toggle in rollouts UI that lets SREs create a "temporary override" with TTL + owner. then surface the audit log link.

kamal: thanks all — will iterate on the PR with token-check, metric labels, and sampling cap. i'll send the draft rule later today. @andrew @sara pls review telemetry/quota parts.
